prompt.en: A CW carrier drifts upward as the cabinet warms. Keying edges were already shaped. Only oscillator mounting and supply stability are improved. Which result is expected?

text.en: Less RF frequency drift; little change to the existing keying-edge spectrum.

feedback.en: The change targets oscillator stability. Edge shaping and harmonic suppression remain separate functions.

text.en: Less key-click energy; little change to the existing RF frequency drift.

feedback.en: Key clicks come from abrupt on-off edges. The stated work targets frequency drift, not edge shaping.

text.en: Less harmonic energy; little change to the existing RF frequency drift.

feedback.en: Harmonics are multiples of the RF frequency. Stabilizing that frequency does not replace harmonic filtering.

text.en: Less RF frequency drift; a wider tuning range set by the keying edges.

feedback.en: Better stability can reduce drift, but keying edges do not set the oscillator tuning range.

explanation.en: Frequency stability, keying-edge shaping, and harmonic filtering address different signal-quality problems. Improving one does not automatically fix the others.

prompt.en: An SSB transmitter has pinned ALC and adjacent-frequency splatter. Which adjustment sequence addresses the likely cause?

text.en: Raise speech processing, then lower speaker volume to judge the result.

feedback.en: More processing can increase average drive and distortion. Speaker volume does not repair the transmitted waveform.

text.en: Raise RF drive, then rely on stronger ALC action to restore waveform shape.

feedback.en: A pinned ALC indication already suggests excessive drive. More limiting is not a substitute for staying inside the clean range.

text.en: Reduce microphone drive and processing, then check voice peaks and a clean-audio report.

feedback.en: Start with less drive and processing. Use the manufacturer's ALC guidance and a clean-signal report, not maximum meter movement.

text.en: Retune the antenna match, then restore the same high audio drive without another report.

feedback.en: A good match does not cure audio overdrive. Recheck transmitted quality after correcting the level.

explanation.en: An SSB signal needs clean linear operation, not maximum meter movement. Excess audio drive or processing can spread unwanted energy into adjacent channels.

prompt.en: A station considers FM with 3.0 kHz peak deviation and 2.7 kHz audio. It must choose between 80 m with a narrow voice bandwidth limit and a suitable wider 10 m channel. Which estimate and plan fit?

text.en: 3.0 kHz; use that FM setup on 80 m because deviation alone sets occupied width.

feedback.en: Deviation is only part of Carson's rule. Including audio and both sides gives a much wider signal.

text.en: 11.4 kHz; use SSB for 80 m and keep that FM setup for the wider 10 m channel.

feedback.en: Carson's rule gives 2 x (3.0 + 2.7) = 11.4 kHz. That wide voice signal does not fit the narrow limit below 28 MHz.

text.en: 5.7 kHz; use that FM setup on 80 m because adding deviation and audio is enough.

feedback.en: The sum is 5.7 kHz, but the rule doubles that sum. Omitting the factor of two understates the bandwidth.

text.en: 6.0 kHz; use that FM setup on 80 m because only twice the deviation counts.

feedback.en: Twice deviation leaves out the highest audio frequency. The estimate must include both terms before doubling.

explanation.en: The occupied-width estimate must come before band choice. Wide FM voice does not fit the narrow voice limits below 28 MHz.
